US Tariff on Danish Retail Goods Hits Industry Firms and Workers

COPENHAGEN, June 12—The Danish retail industry is reporting mounting losses and operational difficulties after the United States imposed a 25% tariff on retail goods imported from Denmark last month, a move industry representatives call a “serious blow” to one of the country’s key export sectors.

The measure, which took effect on May 15, covers a wide range of Danish retail products, including home furnishings, household goods, and apparel. According to the Danish Retail Federation, the US accounted for nearly 12% of Denmark’s retail exports in 2023, making it a crucial market for the sector.

"We are seeing immediate consequences, with shipments being delayed or canceled and inventories piling up," said Mads Eriksen, spokesperson for the Danish Retail Federation. "Several firms have already begun scaling back operations at US-facing distribution sites, and some are considering temporary layoffs."

Among those affected is Nordisk Handel, a large retail chain with export-focused warehouses in Odense and Aarhus. “We estimate a 30% drop in export volume to the US since the tariffs were imposed,” said company representative Louise Jensen. “We have put hiring on hold and may need to reduce working hours for staff at our export centers if the situation persists.”

Local unions report that workers are increasingly concerned about job security. “Employees are worried about possible layoffs or reduced shifts, especially in export-heavy regions,” said Janne Skovgaard, leader of the Retail Workers Union. “We are in talks with management to minimize the impact, but the uncertainty is affecting morale across our sites.”

Industry analysts warn that if the tariffs remain in place, smaller Danish retailers may struggle to absorb the additional costs or find alternative markets quickly. “This is not just a temporary setback,” said trade analyst Henrik Madsen. “The longer the tariffs last, the greater the risk of permanent job losses and closures of export-dependent retail sites.”

The Danish government has called the US action “unjustified” and is seeking dialogue with Washington. In the meantime, industry leaders say they are bracing for further disruptions, with the full impact on firms and workers yet to unfold.
